reasons.reader_question: Clear and specific: what the high court's roll does, and what the queen was about to sign before a recorder could hear it.
reasons.change: The forty's pages are shown powerless and the queen admits the raids before Haran's spears. Her leverage collapses, and Rema shifts power again.
reasons.romance_movement: New reason: Devan witnesses grief for the man who sold Asha's death and his own, and refuses both to argue and to pretend he shares it.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Responsive action throughout: he sits leaving her the curb, palm up and unreaching, touches only when she turns. The goat joke proves shared history.
reasons.character_logic: Precise-counting Neela says 'thirty thousand'. She disclaims bargaining right after setting a condition. 'Always free' ignores Chathu as a living witness.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Accusing the queen with her three hundred spears holding the cut and a three-day truce has a named cost. Haran states it to her face.
reasons.prose: Mostly clean and concrete. Weakened by an orphaned dialogue paragraph, stock lines ('like a stone into a well', 'She never needed to'), and a clunky retcon recap.
reasons.continuity: Consistent with F978, F979, F576, F791, F455 and F521. Some unlisted facts (Chathu taught her letters; who holds the thirty rolls) need logging.

fixes: At "The four leaves you hold are the four guards'": the paragraph is orphaned mid-speech with a redundant tag. Two lines later Neela says "I don't say it to bargain", which contradicts the condition she just set (character logic). Move the four-leaves condition to after the queen's "Yes", as Neela's first answer to it. Keep "The raids made your knives" as her closing line without the bargaining disclaimer.

At "with thirty thousand Thurai on the beach": Neela is defined by exact counts, so a tenfold exaggeration in her most precise speech breaks voice. Haran's correction also deflates the indictment (character logic). Have her say "fourteen hundred Thurai on the beach" herself and cut Haran's line, or give Haran a different interjection that tests her nerve.

At "So the forty are free. They always were.": by the world rules Chathu remains a living witness to all forty turnings. Neela, who knows this (F792), overstates. Add one line conceding it: free of paper, not of one living mouth, and that mouth is now the high court's. This sharpens the queen's "I hold the man" counter and makes Rema's arrival with the roll the answer.
reader_question: What has Justice Rema brought on the high court's roll, and will the queen's 'Yes' and her charter survive being said in front of a recorder?
new_facts_assessment: The listed facts are necessary and consistent. The queen's 'Yes' fits the bible treaty. The four-leaves declaration fits F957 and F998. Haran's 300 matches F914. 'Kept warm as ordered' is a good dangling hook if paid off; otherwise cut it. Unlisted facts to log: Chathu taught Neela her letters (sits beside F360, where Kirri taught the younger girls); Neela holds or has read all thirty crown intake rolls (custody after the burnings is unestablished); 'the widow's coin you paid' (Rema paid it, F520, so say 'your treasury paid'). The truce fact 'runs out in three days' is tautological.
